task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-08-08, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: classifying shapers by cut vs drive tendency
defining shaper roles from play-by-play initiator data
small sample analysis of player styles
assessing differential home-away performance by playing style

historical_evidence.finding: Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves. Gate passed.
The BEST vs AVOID gap is not inflated by games where CUT exceeds 15% of H2 mix. Only 4/272 games had CUT>15%, showing extreme scarcity of cut-heavy possessions.
Named star initiators have identifiable lineup and forced-play-type suppressors in the possession graph. No placebo or matching; later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts.
Teams shift toward HELP/SWITCH and away from DROP in the playoffs; overall no meaningful shift for HELP. Per-team shifts range -0.287 to +0.271 with no test.

failed_approaches.what_failed: test of superstar suppression via lineup and play type
failed_approaches.why: Placebo/matching concerns; later work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts (failure mechanism: E_unclear).

failed_approaches.what_failed: assessing defensive style shift from regular season to playoffs
failed_approaches.why: No meaningful shift detected; per-team ranges wide with no CIs, inconclusive (failure mechanism: E_unclear).

evidence_establishes: The concept of shaper roles is measurable and coverage feasibility is supported.
Cut-heavy possessions are extremely rare at the team-game level (CUT >15% in only 4 of 272 games).
evidence_does_not_establish: No study directly tests whether cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.
Baseline prevalence of cut-heavy vs drive-heavy shapers is unknown.
No validation of play-type classification consistency across home/away contexts.
own_inferences: Given the rarity of cut-heavy team games, cut-heavy shapers are likely very scarce, potentially fewer than 5 in a n=24 shaper sample.
A comparison of home vs away performance (PPP or structural influence) would likely use a correlation or t-test on n=24, yielding very low power.
The term 'travel better' most plausibly refers to smaller decline in performance or role consistency on the road versus at home.
uncertainties: The exact definition of 'travel better' is not specified; it could mean differential home-away PPP, influence stability, or portability across teams.
Classifying shapers requires estimating structural influence, which may need multiple absence spells or large game samples, further shrinking the usable n.
Play-type inferrer accuracy may differ by venue due to tracking data or scorer bias, introducing MEASURE_RELIABILITY concerns.

historical_effect.explanation: No retrieved study tested cut-heavy vs drive-heavy shaper travel; the decision rests entirely on methodological feasibility and the n=24 constraint.

blocking_constraints.text: n=24 shapers overall; splitting into cut-heavy and drive-heavy subgroups yields very small samples, making detection of a realistic effect size unlikely.
Cut-heavy possessions are extremely rare (only 4/272 games with CUT>15% team share), so very few, if any, shapers will qualify as cut-heavy.
Play-type classification (CUT vs DRIVE) may be less accurate for away games if scoring or tracking data differ by venue.

prior_work.summary: Earlier work established that shaper roles can be measured and that cut-heavy possessions are rare. No work addressed role portability by style.

risks.text: With only 24 total shaper units, splitting into cut- and drive-heavy groups likely leaves fewer than 10 per group, severely limiting power.
Cut-heavy shapers may be extremely rare given the low base rate of cut-heavy team games, potentially yielding zero or near-zero cut-heavy observations.
Play type classifications may vary systematically by arena (scoring bias, tracking differences), confounding home/away comparisons.
Classifying shapers based on past cut/drive ratios and then testing future away performance may be affected by regression to the mean.
Team quality, opponent strength, lineup context and game importance differ between home and away and could differ between cut- and drive-heavy shapers.
Testing multiple definitions of travel (PPP, influence, stability) would require multiplicity adjustment, further reducing power.

design.estimand: Difference in away-home performance drop (e.g., PPP or structural influence L_pre) between shapers with a high proportion of CUT initiations and those with a high proportion of DRIVE initiations, controlling for usage and team context.
design.unit: Player-season for shapers with at least 15 games played and at least 200 possessions initiated, separately identified in 2022-23 through 2025-26.
design.sample: All player-seasons classified as Shapers (low usage, positive residual influence) from the structural influence pipeline, with n≈24 expected across the four seasons.
design.power: Assuming 24 shapers, split into two groups of ~12 each, a two-sample t-test at α=0.05 would have 80% power only for an effect size >1.15 standard deviations, unrealistically large for performance differences; actual power is very low.
design.controls: Home/away venue, team offensive rating, opponent defensive rating, teammate quality (average structural influence of other players on the court), game location altitude and travel back-to-back flags.
design.falsification: Placebo test: apply the same home-away comparison to non-shapers (Terminal Scorers, Role Occupants) to check whether any observed difference is specific to shapers or a general artifact. Robustness to alternative cut/drive threshold definitions (tertile split, continuous cut proportion).
design.multiplicity: Pre-specify one primary outcome (away-minus-home PPP) and one secondary (away-minus-home structural influence). Use Bonferroni adjustment.
design.decision_rule: Reject null of no difference between cut-heavy and drive-heavy shapers if two-sided p < 0.05 after adjustment, but acknowledge that power is insufficient to meaningfully interpret a null result.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26 per-game play-by-play, box scores, and derived possession initiator records as of 2026-08-08, with garbage time excluded and minimum 15 possession thresholds per game-half.
